learn.hook: A tiny torch cell has no wires to the wall, yet it can light a bulb. Where does its electricity come from?
points: An electric cell makes electricity from chemicals stored inside it. When the chemicals are used up, the cell stops working.
Every cell has two terminals: a positive (+) terminal, the metal cap, and a negative (−) terminal, the flat metal disc.
A torch bulb has a thin coiled wire called the filament. It glows when electricity flows through it. If the filament breaks, the bulb is 'fused'.
An LED (light emitting diode) has two wires. The longer one goes to the positive side. An LED glows only when connected the right way round.
A switch is a simple device that joins (ON) or breaks (OFF) the path of electricity.

example.q: Raju connects a bulb to a new cell correctly, but it does not glow. Another bulb glows in the same set-up. What is wrong with the first bulb?
steps: The cell is new and works, because another bulb glows.
So the problem is in the first bulb.
Look at its filament: if it is broken, electricity cannot pass through.
example.answer: The first bulb is fused: its filament is broken.

learn.reallife: Torches, TV remotes, wall clocks and toys run on cells. Joining two or more cells together makes a battery, like the one in a mobile phone.

games.title: Match the part to its job
Cell and bulb facts
items: The metal cap of a cell is its positive terminal.
The cap is marked + and the flat disc is −.
A fused bulb has a broken filament.
With the filament broken, the path for electricity is broken.
An LED glows whichever way you connect it.
An LED lets electricity pass only one way, so it must be connected the right way round.
A battery is made by joining two or more cells.
Cells joined + to − make a battery that can give more electricity.
You can safely open a cell to see the chemicals inside.
Cells contain chemicals that can harm you. Never open, burn or break them.

quiz.q: Which part of a torch bulb glows?
quiz.explain: The filament is a thin coiled wire that becomes hot and glows when current passes through it.
steps: A torch bulb has a thin coiled wire called the filament.
The filament glows when electricity flows through it.
The glass, base and wires do not glow.
So the filament glows.
Answer: The filament
quiz.mistake: Thinks the glass itself makes the light

quiz.q: What is the metal cap on top of a cell called?
quiz.explain: The metal cap is the positive (+) terminal. The flat metal disc at the bottom is the negative (−) terminal.
steps: Every cell has two terminals.
The metal cap is the positive (+) terminal; the flat disc is the negative (−).
So the metal cap is the positive terminal.
Answer: Positive terminal
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the positive and negative terminals

quiz.q: Where does a torch cell (dry cell) get its electricity from?
quiz.explain: A cell turns stored chemical energy into electricity. When these chemicals are used up, the cell has to be replaced or recharged.
steps: A cell makes electricity from chemicals stored inside it.
When the chemicals are used up, the cell stops working.
So a dry cell gets electricity from chemicals stored inside it.
Answer: Chemicals stored inside it
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cell is charged by air or light

quiz.q: An LED does not glow even though the cell is new. What is the most likely reason?
options: It is connected the wrong way round
quiz.explain: An LED glows only when its longer leg is connected towards the positive terminal. Turning it around fixes the problem.
steps: An LED glows only when connected the right way round.
Its longer wire must go to the positive side.
A new cell is fine, so the LED must be reversed.
So it is connected the wrong way round.
Answer: It is connected the wrong way round
quiz.mistake: Does not know that an LED works only in one direction

quiz.q: What is a battery?
options: Two or more cells joined together
quiz.explain: In a battery the positive terminal of one cell is joined to the negative terminal of the next.
steps: A battery is made by joining cells.
It is two or more cells joined + to −.
So a battery is two or more cells joined together.
Answer: Two or more cells joined together
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'battery' and 'cell' always mean the same thing

quiz.q: What does a switch do in a circuit?
options: It joins or breaks the path of electricity
It makes the bulb brighter forever
quiz.explain: In the ON position the switch completes the path; in the OFF position it breaks it.
steps: A switch joins (ON) or breaks (OFF) the path of electricity.
It does not make or store electricity.
So it joins or breaks the path of electricity.
Answer: It joins or breaks the path of electricity
quiz.mistake: Thinks a switch is a source of electricity

quiz.q: Which of these is a safe habit?
options: Open old cells to see inside
Put cells in a fire to get rid of them
Touch wires of a wall socket
Never open, burn or play with cells
quiz.explain: Cells contain chemicals, and wall sockets carry dangerous electricity. Old cells should be given for proper disposal.
steps: Cells contain chemicals; wall sockets carry dangerous electricity.
Opening, burning or playing with cells, or touching socket wires, is unsafe.
So the safe habit is never to open, burn or play with cells.
Answer: Never open, burn or play with cells
quiz.mistake: Does not see the danger in cells and sockets

quiz.q: Why does a torch stop glowing after being used for many weeks?
options: The chemicals in its cells are used up
quiz.explain: As the cell works, its chemicals get used up. Then it can no longer push electricity through the bulb.
steps: A cell makes electricity from stored chemicals.
After many weeks of use, these chemicals are used up.
So the torch stops glowing because the chemicals in its cells are used up.
Answer: The chemicals in its cells are used up
quiz.mistake: Thinks cells hold electricity that never runs out

teach.ask: Gappu found a torch cell and a little bulb. What are these parts and how does a cell make the bulb light up?
teach.praise: Chirp! The cell's chemicals push electricity through the filament and it glows. Bright idea, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Which two ends of the cell must the bulb be connected to?

revise.summary: An electric cell makes electricity from stored chemicals and has a positive and a negative terminal. A bulb's filament glows when current flows, an LED glows only the right way round, and a switch joins or breaks the path.
focus: Parts of a bulb and what a fused bulb is
Connecting an LED the right way
What a battery and a switch are
remember: Metal cap = positive (+) terminal; flat disc = negative (−) terminal
Filament = thin coiled wire that glows; broken filament = fused bulb
LED: longer wire goes to the positive side
Battery = two or more cells joined + to −
traps: A new cell with a dark bulb may mean the bulb is fused, not the cell.
An LED will not glow if connected the wrong way round.
Never open, burn or play with cells.

learn.hook: Electricity is like a racing track: it only flows if the track is a complete loop with no gaps!
points: A circuit is a complete, closed path for electricity: from the positive terminal of the cell, through wires and a bulb, back to the negative terminal.
If there is any gap, the circuit is open (or broken) and the bulb does not glow.
A switch in the ON position closes the circuit. In the OFF position it opens it.
Scientists draw circuits using symbols. In a cell symbol, the longer thin line is the positive terminal and the shorter thick line is the negative terminal.
A circuit diagram is quick to draw and easy for anyone in the world to read.

example.q: A bulb is joined to a cell with two wires, but both wires touch only the positive terminal. Will the bulb glow?
steps: For the bulb to glow, electricity must flow through a complete loop.
The loop must go from the positive terminal, through the bulb, to the negative terminal.
Here the negative terminal is not connected, so the path is not complete.
example.answer: No. The circuit is open, because the negative terminal is not connected.

learn.reallife: When you press the switch of a fan at home, you complete a circuit. Electricians read circuit diagrams to wire buildings safely.

Back to the negative terminal of the cell

quiz.q: What is a closed circuit?
options: A circuit kept in a closed box
A complete path for electricity with no gaps
A circuit with the switch OFF
quiz.explain: Electricity flows only through a complete loop. 'Closed' means the loop has no gap.
steps: Electricity flows only through a complete loop.
A closed circuit has no gaps from + terminal back to − terminal.
So a closed circuit is a complete path for electricity with no gaps.
Answer: A complete path for electricity with no gaps
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'closed' means the switch is turned off, like closing a tap

quiz.q: The switch in a circuit is OFF. What happens?
options: The circuit is open and the bulb does not glow
quiz.explain: OFF means the switch has made a gap in the path, so no current flows.
steps: OFF means the switch makes a gap in the path.
A gap makes the circuit open, so no current flows.
So the circuit is open and the bulb does not glow.
Answer: The circuit is open and the bulb does not glow
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the meanings of open and closed circuits

quiz.q: In the circuit symbol of a cell, which line shows the positive terminal?
quiz.explain: By agreement the longer thin line is positive (+) and the shorter thick line is negative (−).
steps: In the cell symbol, two lines are drawn.
The longer thin line is positive (+); the shorter thick line is negative (−).
So the longer, thinner line is positive.
Answer: The longer, thinner line
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the long and short lines of the cell symbol

quiz.q: Why do we use symbols to draw circuits?
options: They are quick to draw and understood everywhere
They are needed to make a bulb glow
quiz.explain: Standard symbols let anyone, anywhere, read a circuit diagram without drawing real-looking pictures.
steps: Circuit symbols are standard.
They are quick to draw and anyone in the world can read them.
So we use them because they are quick and understood everywhere.
Answer: They are quick to draw and understood everywhere
quiz.mistake: Thinks a diagram itself affects the circuit

quiz.q: A bulb's two wires are both connected to the negative terminal of a cell. Does it glow?
options: No, because the circuit is not complete
Only if the switch is OFF
quiz.explain: Electricity must go from one terminal through the bulb to the other terminal. Here the positive terminal is left out.
steps: A complete circuit goes from one terminal, through the bulb, to the other terminal.
Here both wires touch only the negative terminal.
The positive terminal is left out, so the circuit is not complete.
So No, the bulb does not glow.
Answer: No, because the circuit is not complete
quiz.mistake: Thinks touching the cell anywhere is enough

quiz.q: In a working circuit, electricity is said to flow from:
options: The negative terminal to the bulb only
The bulb into the cell's cap and stops there
The positive terminal, round the circuit, to the negative terminal
quiz.explain: In circuit diagrams we show current leaving the positive terminal and returning to the negative terminal.
steps: A circuit is a closed path from the positive terminal back to the negative terminal.
Current is shown leaving + and returning to −.
So electricity flows from the positive terminal, round the circuit, to the negative terminal.
Answer: The positive terminal, round the circuit, to the negative terminal
quiz.mistake: Thinks current goes out and stops instead of flowing in a loop

quiz.q: Sana's bulb flickers when she shakes her circuit. What is the most likely cause?
options: The switch is missing a symbol
quiz.explain: A loose wire keeps making and breaking the path, so the bulb flickers on and off.
steps: Shaking makes the bulb go on and off.
A loose wire keeps making and breaking the path.
So the likely cause is a loose connection.
Answer: A loose connection
quiz.mistake: Does not connect flickering with a path that keeps opening and closing

quiz.q: To make a bulb glow brighter in a torch, two cells are placed one after the other. How should they be joined?
options: Positive terminal of one to negative terminal of the other
quiz.explain: Cells in a battery are joined + to −. If they face the same way like this, they work together.
steps: In a battery, cells are joined + to −.
So the positive terminal of one cell touches the negative terminal of the next.
Then they work together to make the bulb brighter.
Answer: Positive terminal of one to negative terminal of the other
quiz.mistake: Puts cells the wrong way, so they work against each other

teach.ask: Gappu joined a bulb to a cell with wires, but it won't glow! What does Gappu need for electricity to flow?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! A complete closed loop from + to −. Gappu's bulb is shining!
teach.nudge: Is the path for electricity complete, with no gaps?

revise.summary: A circuit is a complete, closed path for electricity from the positive terminal, through the bulb, back to the negative terminal. Any gap makes it open. Circuits are drawn with standard symbols.
focus: How a switch opens and closes a circuit
Reading circuit symbols, especially the cell
remember: Closed circuit = complete path with no gaps
Switch ON closes the circuit; OFF opens it
Cell symbol: longer thin line = +, shorter thick line = −
Current is shown going from + round the circuit to −
traps: Both wires on the same terminal do not make a circuit.
Don't mix up the cell symbol lines: the longer one is positive.
A flickering bulb usually means a loose connection.

learn.hook: Why does the screwdriver of an electrician have a plastic or rubber handle? Let's find out!
points: Materials that let electricity pass through them easily are called conductors. Metals like copper, aluminium and iron are good conductors.
Materials that do not let electricity pass easily are called insulators, like rubber, plastic, dry wood, glass and dry paper.
Graphite (the 'lead' of a pencil) is not a metal, but it conducts electricity.
Wires have a copper or aluminium core covered with a plastic coat. The metal carries the current; the plastic keeps us safe.
Our body can conduct electricity, so never touch switches with wet hands or play near electric poles. The mains supply in Indian homes is about 230 volts, which is dangerous.

example.q: You make a tester: a cell, a bulb and two wires with a gap. You touch both free ends to a steel spoon and the bulb glows. Then you try a plastic ruler and it does not. What do you conclude?
steps: The bulb glows only if the object completes the circuit.
The steel spoon completed it: it lets current pass.
The plastic ruler did not: it blocks current.
example.answer: Steel (a metal) is a conductor; plastic is an insulator.

learn.reallife: Electricians wear rubber gloves and rubber-soled shoes, and switch boards are made of plastic, because these are insulators.

items.text: A wire has a metal core covered with ___ for safety.
Graphite is a non-metal that is a ___ of electricity.
Never touch a switch with ___ hands.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good conductor of electricity?
quiz.explain: Copper is a metal, and metals conduct electricity well. That is why most wires are made of copper.
steps: Conductors let electricity pass easily.
Metals like copper are good conductors.
Rubber, plastic and glass are insulators.
So copper is a good conductor.
Answer: Copper
quiz.mistake: Does not know which materials conduct

quiz.q: Which material is an insulator?
quiz.explain: Dry wood does not let electricity pass easily. Aluminium and iron are metals, and graphite conducts too.
steps: Insulators do not let electricity pass easily.
Dry wood is an insulator.
Aluminium and iron are metals, and graphite conducts too.
So dry wood is the insulator.
Answer: Dry wood
quiz.mistake: Thinks graphite is an insulator because it is not a metal

quiz.q: Why are electric wires covered with plastic?
options: Plastic is an insulator and protects us from shocks
quiz.explain: The copper or aluminium inside carries the current. The plastic covering stops it from reaching our hands.
steps: The metal core of a wire carries the current.
Plastic is an insulator, so it stops current reaching our hands.
So wires are covered with plastic to protect us from shocks.
Answer: Plastic is an insulator and protects us from shocks
quiz.mistake: Thinks the plastic coat helps carry the current

quiz.q: Which non-metal conducts electricity?
quiz.explain: Graphite, a form of carbon found in pencil 'lead', conducts electricity although it is a non-metal.
steps: Most non-metals do not conduct electricity.
Graphite (pencil 'lead') is a non-metal that does conduct.
So the answer is graphite.
Answer: Graphite
quiz.mistake: Believes no non-metal can ever conduct electricity

quiz.q: You touch the two free wires of a tester to a safety pin and the bulb glows. The safety pin is:
quiz.explain: The bulb glows because current passed through the pin. So the pin conducts electricity.
steps: In the tester, the bulb glows only if current passes through the object.
The bulb glowed with the safety pin.
So the safety pin is a conductor.
Answer: A conductor
quiz.mistake: Mixes up conductor and insulator

quiz.q: Why is it dangerous to touch a switch with wet hands?
options: Water on hands can let electricity pass into the body
Switches only work when dry hands touch them
quiz.explain: Ordinary water carries electricity easily enough to give a dangerous shock through wet skin.
steps: Our body can conduct electricity.
Water on wet hands lets electricity pass into the body more easily.
So never touch switches with wet hands.
Answer: Water on hands can let electricity pass into the body
quiz.mistake: Does not know that our body and ordinary water can conduct electricity

quiz.q: What is the mains supply voltage in Indian homes?
quiz.explain: Homes in India get about 230 volts, which can kill. A torch cell gives only about 1.5 volts, which is safe for experiments.
steps: The mains supply in Indian homes is about 230 volts.
This is dangerous; a torch cell gives only about 1.5 volts.
So the answer is about 230 volts.
Answer: About 230 volts
quiz.mistake: Thinks home electricity is as weak as a torch cell

quiz.q: An electrician's screwdriver has a plastic handle because:
options: Plastic makes the screw turn faster
quiz.explain: The insulating handle stops current from flowing into the electrician's hand.
steps: The handle must stop current from reaching the hand.
Plastic is an insulator.
So the screwdriver has a plastic handle because plastic is an insulator.
Answer: Plastic is an insulator
quiz.mistake: Confuses conductors and insulators

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know: why are wires shiny metal inside but covered with plastic outside?
teach.praise: Chirp! Metal carries the current, plastic keeps fingers safe. Smart wiring, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Which kind of material lets electricity through, and which blocks it?

revise.summary: Conductors like metals let electricity pass easily; insulators like rubber, plastic, dry wood and glass do not. Graphite is a non-metal conductor. Our body conducts too, so we must stay safe.
focus: Sorting materials into conductors and insulators
Testing materials with a simple tester
Why wires and tool handles have plastic coverings
remember: Insulators: rubber, plastic, dry wood, glass, dry paper
Indian home mains ≈ 230 volts (dangerous); torch cell ≈ 1.5 volts
Never touch switches with wet hands
traps: Don't say all non-metals are insulators; graphite conducts.
Don't think plastic carries the current in a wire; the metal core does.
